api.name: DataBank
api.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: DataBank announced a $250 million TJC investment and an approximately $600 million secondary share sale; DigitalBridge disclosed that the transaction would adjust its continuing DataBank stake to 7.8%.

DataBank announced an approximately $2.0 billion equity raise led by AustralianSuper's $1.5 billion commitment, which would make AustralianSuper a significant minority owner; DataBank now lists it as a current investor.

Colony Capital purchased $185 million of secondary DataBank interests from Edgewater and Allstate; Edgewater exited, Allstate retained half of its prior interest and the Nuveen-branded TIAA investment continued.
Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners with TIAA, Allstate Investments and The Edgewater Funds, launching its first data-center platform.
DataBank Ltd. was founded in the former Federal Reserve Bank Building in downtown Dallas, Texas.

A Swiss Life-led consortium with EDF Invest, Northleaf and Ardian closed a collective 35% DataBank interest for approximately $1.5 billion; IMCO then agreed to invest up to $450 million in the continuing recapitalization.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Mosaic Forest Management is a Canadian timberlands and land-management platform overseeing the TimberWest and Island Timberlands interests across Vancouver Island and coastal British Columbia.

The business manages sustainable forestry, timber production and related land uses, including renewable-energy, watershed, recreation, real-estate and carbon initiatives. Mosaic launched on November 1, 2018. BCI remains the in-scope infrastructure owner through its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program and reported a 56.1% interest in Mosaic LP at year-end 2025. PSP Investments remains the other legal owner through its Natural Resources mandate; its exact published percentage is not publicly disclosed, and it is not treated as a PSP Infrastructure holding. AIMCo participated at launch but was no longer named in Mosaic's 2024 statutory ownership report, so it is preserved as a former owner with an undisclosed exit date.

STORY TIMELINE
Nov 1, 2018
Investment

BCI-, PSP- and AIMCo-affiliated owners launched Mosaic Forest Management to manage the TimberWest and Island Timberlands businesses as one platform.

2011
Acquisition

BCI and PSP Investments acquired TimberWest, establishing one of the two predecessor ownership groups later managed through Mosaic.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Nexus Water Group, Inc. is a regulated water and wastewater utility platform formed when the U.S. regulated operations of Corix Infrastructure combined with SouthWest Water Company on April 1, 2024. The business operates locally branded systems across the United States and Canada and serves more than 1.3 million people. BCI owns 50.0% through its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program. The other 50% is held through SWMAC Holdco, producing indirect platform interests of 37.5% for J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund and 12.5% for a Munich Re vehicle managed by MEAG. Nexus completed the sale of systems in eight states to American Water on June 1, 2026, while its announced Nevada and Oregon asset sale remained pending; neither transaction is a sponsor sale or platform exit.

STORY TIMELINE
Jun 1, 2026
Divestiture

American Water completed its purchase of Nexus systems in eight states; the transaction was an asset divestiture and did not change ownership of the Nexus platform.

Feb 25, 2026
Divestiture

Nexus agreed to sell its Nevada and Oregon systems to California Water Service Group; the asset sale remained pending regulatory approval in the buyer's July 29, 2026 filing.

Founding

The U.S. regulated water and wastewater businesses of Corix Infrastructure and SouthWest Water combined to form Nexus Water Group.

Apr 1, 2024
Investment

BCI's Corix interests and the IIF/Bazos-backed SouthWest platform completed their combination, establishing the 50% BCI and 50% SWMAC ownership structure.

Jun 14, 2018
Acquisition

MEAG completed a 25% investment in predecessor SouthWest Water on behalf of Munich Re, an interest later carried into Nexus through Bazos and SWMAC Holdco.
